numerical_failure.observed_behavior: For native complex arrays containing NaN in either the real or imaginary component, `array_equivalent` returns `False` for the `dtype_equal=True` case while the `dtype_equal=False` comparison returns `True` (self-inconsistent). It also causes `Series.equals` to return `False` where it should return `True` when both elements are NA.
numerical_failure.expected_behavior: `array_equivalent` should treat complex values as NA if either their real or imaginary part is NaN, and it should therefore consider two elements equivalent when both are NA even if their non-NaN components differ. This should match the `dtype_equal=False` path exactly, and make `Series.equals` return `True` in the described NA case.
trigger_conditions: Input arrays have native complex dtype (`left.dtype.kind == 'c'`).
At least one complex element has NaN in either its real or imaginary component.
The fastpath that views complex arrays as float pairs is taken (i.e., native complex previously reached the complex pair-view path).

input_output_examples.expected_output: dtype_equal=False and dtype_equal=True should be consistent (equivalence should be True when both elements are NA per whole-element isna semantics).

input_output_examples.input: Series.equals with identical-dtype NA complex elements where both elements are NA

oracle_clues: A complex value is NA if either its real or imaginary part is NaN; whole-element isna semantics are required for correctness (GH#66160).

The fix changes the implementation to use numpy’s whole-element complex `np.isnan` logic: `((left == right) | (np.isnan(left) & np.isnan(right))).all()` and drops the complex pair-view fastpath that compared real/imag independently.
The observed discrepancy is explicitly that the fastpath disagreed with the `dtype_equal=False` path and broke `Series.equals` consistency.

numerical_characteristics.dtype: complex (native complex, kinds 'c16'/'c8' and byte-endianness variants '>c16'/' >c8')
category_specific_evidence: Complex NA semantics: “a complex value is NA if either part is NaN” (PR#66323, commit message, and test comment).

Where it enters: array_equivalent’s float fastpath viewed complex as float pairs (complex128 -> float64, complex64 -> float32), comparing real/imag parts independently, which breaks whole-element NA semantics (PR#66323, commit message, diff in missing.py).
Special values involved: NaN (real-part NaN or imaginary-part NaN). Evidence does not mention +/-inf, signed zero, or subnormals.

Correct handling: route complex through the numpy comparison using whole-element isna: `((left == right) | (np.isnan(left) & np.isnan(right))).all()`, with `np.isnan` on complex “reports whole-element NA” and matches the `dtype_equal=False` path (PR#66323, missing.py diff).

Test coverage for NaN in components: `left=np.array([complex(1, np.nan)])` vs `right=np.array([complex(2, np.nan)])` and `left=np.array([complex(np.nan, 1)])` vs `right=np.array([complex(np.nan, 2)])`, asserting `array_equivalent(..., dtype_equal=...)` (test_missing.py).
